clue.text: Repellent figure on the field in dreadful soccer war

indicators.note: dreadful suggests something in a terrible mess, so the letters of these two words are jumbled

explanation.surface: A grim football clash is pictured, with something scary standing on the pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dreadful' rearranges the nine letters of SOCCER WAR. The 'field' looks like a football pitch but is farmland.
explanation.definitionFit: A stuffed effigy stands in crops to frighten birds away, a figure that repels them.

clue.text: As a type of sentence, it doesn't mean hanging

definitions.text: As a type of sentence, it doesn't mean hanging

parts.words: As a type of sentence, it doesn't mean hanging
parts.note: a court can order a jail term that is only served if the offender reoffends; the same word normally means dangling, yet here no gallows is meant

explanation.definitionFit: A suspended sentence is one not enforced unless further offences occur, though the word otherwise means hung up.

clue.text: It's placed above the green as a warning to those driving off

definitions.text: It's placed above the green as a warning to those driving off

parts.words: It's placed above the green as a warning to those driving off
parts.note: the golf words green and driving off point to a course, but the scene is a road junction with signals

explanation.definitionFit: On British traffic lights the caution colour sits above green and warns motorists the signal will change.

clue.text: Play all the hands

definitions.meaning: a medieval English morality drama whose hero stands for all humanity
every worker, each person on the crew

explanation.definitionFit: Everyman is the title of a fifteenth-century morality drama; split, it means each and every person.

clue.text: Unfaithful man angered distraught sweetheart

indicators.note: distraught means deeply upset, so the letters of the word before are thrown into disorder

parts.note: the heart, or middle letter, of the word sweet is E

explanation.surface: A jealous lover rages at a cheating partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distraught' rearranges ANGERED to RENEGAD; 'sweetheart' is the middle letter of SWEET.
explanation.definitionFit: A turncoat deserts a cause or faith, so is disloyal.

clue.text: Pursuing ducks in flight

indicators.note: in places the two round letters inside the word for flight

parts.note: wing means flight, as in taking wing
in cricket a duck is a score of nought, so two ducks are two Os

explanation.surface: A hunter chases birds as they fly off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ducks' are birds in the surface but cricket noughts, O and O, here.
explanation.definitionFit: Courting someone romantically is going after them.

clue.text: No quiet in university area for author

indicators.note: No tells us to go without the letter for quiet, removing it from the word before it

parts.note: a campus is the grounds of a university
p, piano, is the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: Someone seeks a silent spot on a college site to find a writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No' removes P (piano, quiet in music) from CAMPUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Albert Camus was the French writer of The Outsider and The Plague.

clue.text: Keen to gather in woman's fruit

indicators.note: to gather in means to enclose, so the word for keen wraps round the other piece

parts.note: to keen is to wail or cry in mourning
her is a woman's, the female possessive

explanation.surface: Someone is eager to harvest a lady's crop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keen' looks like an adjective meaning eager; it is the verb to wail.
explanation.definitionFit: A small round stone fruit, red when ripe, grown on trees.

clue.text: Time when waist span becomes apparent?

definitions.text: Time when waist span becomes apparent?

parts.words: Time when waist span becomes apparent?
parts.note: a play on the spreading paunch said to come with the years between youth and old age

explanation.definitionFit: Middle-age spread is the thickening waistline associated with one's forties and fifties.

clue.text: Knowing about a daughter in unfortunate way

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for knowing goes round the other letters

parts.note: sly means knowing or artful

explanation.surface: A shrewd remark about a daughter is made in an unlucky fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts SLY around A and D.
explanation.definitionFit: Regrettably and unfortunately are near synonyms for an adverb of misfortune.

clue.text: Churchman bishop and 'e met separately in African state

indicators.note: in places the second letter inside the country's name as well
separately says the two letters go into the country apart from each other, not as one block

parts.note: Sudan is a country in north-east Africa
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
'e is he with the h dropped, as in Cockney speech, leaving the letter E

explanation.surface: A bishop and some fellow meet up, each on his own, somewhere in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'separately in' puts B and E into SUDAN at different places, SU-B-D-E-AN; 'met' is padding for the picture of two people meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: A subdean is a clergyman ranking just below a dean in a cathedral.

clue.text: Section of Rigoletto Verdi definitely carried too far

indicators.note: Section of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A passage from Verdi's opera Rigoletto is accused of being over the top.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across rigolettO VERDI DefInitely.
explanation.definitionFit: To overdo is to take something to excess, so the past tense means took it too far.

clue.text: Start off almost too soon

indicators.note: Start off means the opening letter of the word for almost is taken away

parts.note: nearly means almost

explanation.surface: Someone sets off a little before time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start off' drops the first letter, N, from NEARLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Arriving before the appointed time is arriving prematurely.

clue.text: Commander takes 11 without 20, as a rule

parts.note: a general is a senior army commander

indicators.note: without means the letters of one entry are taken away from the other

parts.note: the answer to 11 across, meaning too soon
20 across is clued as an organ one listens with, the ear, which opens that answer

explanation.surface: An army leader absorbs some cross-references and behaves according to habit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' takes EAR (the organ in 20's clue, also the start of its answer) from EARLY, leaving LY.
explanation.definitionFit: Generally and as a rule both mean usually, in most cases.

clue.text: Breaks up underworld gangs

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld, and his realm
bands are groups or gangs

explanation.surface: Police smash criminal gangs from the underworld.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'Breaks up' as police action and 'underworld' as crime; here it is the classical realm of the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: To disband a group is to dissolve or dismiss it.

clue.text: Coastline spoilt in parts

indicators.note: spoilt means ruined, so the letters of the word before are wrecked into a new order

explanation.surface: A stretch of shore has been damaged in places.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spoilt' rearranges COASTLINE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something made in sections or pieces is described this way, like modular furniture.

clue.text: Said to change ends on platform

indicators.note: to change ends asks for the first and last letters of the word to swap places

explanation.surface: A speaker on a stage is reported to switch from one end to the other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to change ends' swaps the S and D of SAID. The definition is 'platform'; 'on' tells you the answer sits in that position.
explanation.definitionFit: A dais is a raised stage at one end of a hall for speakers.

clue.text: Ancient mariner to return fire

parts.note: to shell is to fire artillery at
back means return, as in to go back

explanation.surface: An old sailor is told to shoot back at his attackers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to return fire' is the phrase 'to shell back' with its halves in the clue the other way round. Ancient Mariner recalls Coleridge's poem.
explanation.definitionFit: A shellback is slang for an old, experienced seaman, especially one who has crossed the equator.

clue.text: Becoming liberal

definitions.meaning: generous, as in a large sum given freely

explanation.definitionFit: Handsome means good-looking and also ample, as in a generous gift.

clue.text: Why, we hear, letter's about an architectural feature

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for letter goes round the other piece

parts.note: an epistle is a letter, as in the New Testament; the 's is is, a link

indicators.note: we hear says a word is spoken, and its sound is written as a single letter

parts.note: the question word why is spoken like the letter Y

explanation.surface: Someone asks why a letter concerns a building detail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' turns WHY into the letter Y, which 'about' places inside EPISTLE.
explanation.definitionFit: An epistyle is the architrave, the beam resting on top of classical columns.

clue.text: Make ornate cards

definitions.meaning: a full pack of playing cards

explanation.definitionFit: To deck is to adorn something; a pack of playing cards is also called this.

clue.text: One listens through this organ composition

parts.note: the ear is the organ of hearing
a piece is a musical composition

explanation.surface: A listener hears an organ work played.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organ' suggests the instrument, fitting 'composition', but it is the body part.
explanation.definitionFit: A headphone or receiver held to the head is what a listener hears sound through.

clue.text: Old ship, say, if not a fleet

definitions.meaning: a large merchant sailing vessel of the sixteenth century
a whole flotilla of such trading vessels

explanation.definitionFit: An argosy was a big Renaissance trading vessel, and the word also names a fleet of them.

clue.text: Striking obstruction in opening

parts.note: workers who are striking are out
a let is a hindrance, as in without let or hindrance

explanation.surface: A blocking shot is played at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Striking' means on strike; 'obstruction' recalls the legal phrase 'without let or hindrance'.
explanation.definitionFit: An outlet is a vent or exit through which something can escape.

clue.text: Turn suddenly to make a collection

definitions.meaning: to spin quickly to face the other way
an informal gathering of money from colleagues, say for a leaving gift

explanation.definitionFit: Whip round is a sharp about-turn; a whip-round is money pooled by a group for a present.

clue.text: Grown in a way that's twisted or crooked

indicators.note: twisted means bent out of shape, so the letters of the word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A plant has grown bent and misshapen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twisted' rearranges GROWN; 'in a way that's' and 'or' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrong and crooked both mean dishonest or not right.

clue.text: Stonewall, wanting nothing new?

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so these letters are taken out of the word before

parts.note: O, the round figure zero, means nothing
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone resists change, digging in against anything novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanting' takes O and NEW out of STONEWALL. The whole clue also defines: to delay because you want no change.
explanation.definitionFit: To stall is to play for time or obstruct progress, much as a cricketer blocks every ball.

clue.text: Little boy reportedly gets a top mark

indicators.note: reportedly means as said aloud, so a name stands for the letters with the same sound

parts.note: Alf is a short form of the boy's name Alfred

explanation.surface: A young lad is said to earn the highest grade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' turns ALF into ALPH, then A is added; a little boy is a short name, not a child.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpha, the first Greek letter, is the highest grade on some marking scales.

clue.text: Personal ambition that unintentionally helps the opposition

parts.note: own means personal, belonging to oneself
a goal is an aim or ambition

explanation.surface: A selfish aim backfires and benefits rivals.
explanation.walkthrough: The football sense hides behind 'ambition'; the clue also reads as a whole description of a self-defeating act.
explanation.definitionFit: In football, putting the ball into your own net scores for the other side; figuratively, any self-harming act.

clue.text: Sporting venue — Oval? I'm involved with play there

parts.note: an oval is shaped like the letter O

indicators.note: involved suggests entangled, so these pieces are mixed up together

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether the Oval, the London cricket ground, is where they are performing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oval' suggests THE OVAL, a London cricket ground, but gives only O; with IM and PLAY it is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Olympia in Greece hosted the ancient Games, and London's Olympia hall stages horse shows.

clue.text: Doll's expression conveying surprise

definitions.meaning: a soft rag doll; the 's is is, so the clue says this is a doll
a mild exclamation of astonishment, like gosh

explanation.definitionFit: A golly was a once-popular black-faced rag doll; the word is also a mild oath of amazement.

clue.text: Leisure area could be burden to explorer

parts.note: the burden of a song or argument is its main theme
Mungo Park was a Scottish explorer of the Niger

explanation.surface: A load might weigh down an adventurer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'burden' looks like a heavy load, but it means the chief subject or refrain.
explanation.definitionFit: An amusement venue with rides built round a single subject is a place for recreation.
